summary: Defines encoding instructions that can be added to an ASN.1 specification to change how values are encoded by RXER and its canonical form, such as encoding a component as an XML attribute rather than a child element. It is an experimental protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: Extra notes on a form can tell the XML converter how to write each field. This note defines those notes.

questions: how to encode an asn.1 component as an xml attribute
how to encode asn.1 component as xml attribute
how to reference external xml schemas in asn.1
subtitle: How to customize the XML encoding of ASN.1 data structures.

tldr.problem: RXER (Robust XML Encoding Rules) is a comprehensive standard for encoding ASN.1 as XML, but applications often need fine-grained control over how values are encoded—for example, encoding a field as an XML attribute instead of a child element, or incorporating schema elements from other XML technologies.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4911 defines 14 categories of encoding instructions (24 specific instructions total) that can be added to ASN.1 specifications as type prefixes or in encoding control sections. These instructions tell the RXER encoder exactly how to handle each component: as attributes, elements, lists, with custom names, in specific namespaces, or by reference to external schema declarations.
tldr.outcome: ASN.1 specifications can now precisely control RXER encoding, achieve semantic equivalence with XML Schema or RELAX NG definitions, and even incorporate external schema fragments directly into ASN.1 definitions.

facts.label: Instruction categories
facts.value: Component, reference, schema, expansion, and insertion instructions

today: RFC 4911 is an Experimental protocol and remains experimental. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RXER (Robust XML Encoding Rules) encodes ASN.1 values as XML. Unlike simpler encoding rules, RXER allows fine-grained control over the XML output through encoding instructions—optional directives added to ASN.1 specifications that modify encoding behavior.

This RFC defines the notation and semantics of RXER encoding instructions. It also addresses a broader purpose: it allows ASN.1 specifications to incorporate type definitions from other XML schema languages (XML Schema, RELAX NG, DTD) directly, enabling RXER to serve as a bridge between ASN.1 and the broader XML ecosystem.

Encoding instructions can appear as type prefixes (affecting a single component) or in encoding control sections (affecting components across the specification). Each instruction is self-contained and independent.
sections.plainLanguage: RXER turns ASN.1 data into XML. But before encoding, you can add notes saying things like 'use an attribute instead of an element' or 'this field is really an XML Schema type.' This RFC defines all those notes.

sections.title: Categories of Encoding Instructions
sections.content:
RXER encoding instructions fall into several categories:

Component instructions control how individual named components are encoded: ATTRIBUTE (as XML attribute), ELEMENT (as child element), NAME (with a custom name), LIST (as space-separated values), SIMPLE-CONTENT (embed in text), UNION (pick by type), GROUP (group related components), VALUES (rename enumeration values), and insertion instructions (version indicators, type prefixes).

Reference instructions allow components to be constrained by or reference external definitions: ATTRIBUTE-REF (reference XML attribute declaration), ELEMENT-REF (reference element declaration), COMPONENT-REF (reference another ASN.1 component), TYPE-REF (reference an external type), REF-AS-ELEMENT/TYPE (bind to external elements or types).

Schema instructions provide module-level control: SCHEMA-IDENTITY (set schema identity), TARGET-NAMESPACE (set namespace URI and prefix).

Expansion instructions control namespace handling: importing element and attribute declarations from other schemas.
sections.plainLanguage: The instructions are grouped by what they do: some say how to encode one field, some reference external schema definitions, some set module-wide defaults, and some handle complex scenarios like versioning and groups.

sections.title: Component Encoding Instructions
sections.content:
The most common encoding instructions are component instructions, which attach to individual named components:

ATTRIBUTE: Encode the component as an XML attribute instead of an element. Restricted to types that serialize as simple values (strings, numbers, etc.; not CHOICE, SET, or unrestricted SEQUENCE OF).

NAME: Override the component's XML element or attribute name, either with a literal name or a case transformation (capitalize, uncapitalize, uppercase, lowercase).

LIST: Encode a SEQUENCE OF or SET OF as a space-separated list within a single element, rather than separate child elements.

ELEMENT-REF / ATTRIBUTE-REF: Encode the component as an element or attribute whose name and constraints come from an external XML Schema, RELAX NG, or DTD definition, referenced by qualified name.

COMPONENT-REF: Treat this component as if it were a different top-level component defined elsewhere, inheriting its name and structure.

SIMPLE-CONTENT: For a complex type, embed the content as text rather than structured elements.

UNION: When encoding a CHOICE, indicate the chosen alternative by a wrapper element (rather than by position).
sections.plainLanguage: These instructions say things like 'encode this as an attribute,' 'call it "foo" instead of the default name,' 'make a space-separated list,' or 'treat it like this other component.'

sections.title: Referencing External Schemas
sections.content:
A key feature of RXER encoding instructions is the ability to reference external schema definitions, bridging ASN.1 with XML Schema, RELAX NG, and DTDs:

ELEMENT-REF and ATTRIBUTE-REF reference element and attribute declarations from external schemas. The reference uses a qualified name (namespace + local name) and optionally a context URI to disambiguate when multiple schemas define the same names. Encoding these references restricts the ASN.1 value to conform to the referenced declaration's type.

TYPE-REF and REF-AS-TYPE allow binding ASN.1 types to definitions in external schemas. A value encoded with TYPE-REF conforms to the referenced type; REF-AS-TYPE encodes it using the external type's serialization.

COMPONENT-REF references another top-level named component within ASN.1 itself, creating a kind of type alias. This is useful for sharing complex structures without duplicating definitions.

These reference instructions enable RXER to consume and produce XML that is validated against arbitrary XML schemas, making ASN.1 specifications compatible with the broader XML ecosystem.
sections.plainLanguage: You can say 'this ASN.1 field must match the XML Schema definition of foo.xsd:Bar' or 'this field is really the same structure as that other component.' It's like importing definitions.

sections.title: Advanced Features: Versioning, Grouping, and Insertions
sections.content:
Beyond basic component control, RXER provides instructions for advanced scenarios:

TYPE-AS-VERSION: Embed type version information in the encoded output, supporting protocol versioning by allowing extensions to be decoded with type knowledge.

VERSION-INDICATOR: Add version fields to the encoding for tracking which extensions are present.

GROUP: Logically group related components for versioning and extension support, with rules for unambiguous encoding (ensuring the decoder can always determine which variant is present).

Insertion instructions (ATTRIBUTE, ELEMENT): Insert additional elements or attributes (versions, type tags, or custom markup) into the encoded output.

These features enable RXER-encoded data to evolve over time, support multiple protocol versions, and carry type information needed for successful decoding of extensions and variants.
sections.plainLanguage: For evolving protocols that need to stay backward compatible, these instructions let you mark versions, group changes, and embed information that helps future decoders understand new extensions.

sections.title: Security and Status
sections.content:
An ASN.1 specification with RXER encoding instructions produces RXER encodings that are semantically equivalent to those of the same specification without instructions (the instructions just customize the output). The security properties of the underlying ASN.1 types and data are unchanged by encoding instructions.

The RFC defines strict rules on which instruction combinations are allowed and which types can be subject to which instructions. These restrictions ensure deterministic encoding and decoding.

RFC 4911 is an Experimental protocol from 2007 and remains experimental. It has not been obsoleted or updated.
sections.plainLanguage: The instructions just control how the XML looks; they do not change what the data means or how safe it is to use.
